findings.title: Negative offsets passed to Django queryset slicing raise errors
findings.body: When advanced features are enabled and cursor.offset < 0, the code calls queryset[start_offset:stop] with a negative start. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing and raise ValueError/AssertionError, so a crafted cursor turns into a 500. The comment saying "the ORM handles negative slicing automatically" is false.

findings.title: BasePaginator now passes negative offsets through for prev cursors
findings.body: For prev cursors, start_offset is set to the raw offset with no clamping. Cursor.from_string accepts negative offsets, so a user-supplied cursor like '123:-5:1' leads to negative queryset slicing on every endpoint that uses BasePaginator. That raises an exception and returns a 500. The previous behaviour also passed the offset through, but the new comment claims this is safe, which it is not; the offset should be clamped or rejected.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot handle datetime keys
findings.body: get_item_key calls math.floor/ceil on the key value, and value_from_cursor returns the raw number. The audit log endpoint orders this paginator by `datetime`, so math.floor on a datetime raises TypeError and the cursor number is compared against a datetime column. The optimized path fails on any non-empty result.

findings.title: organization_context.member may be None
findings.body: For superusers or staff who are not members of the organization, organization_context.member is None. Because `or` is evaluated left to right, superusers short-circuit and are fine. However, any non-superuser request without a membership raises AttributeError on `.has_global_access`, and that happens even when optimized_pagination was not requested.

findings.title: span_count can be stale after the second zunionstore is skipped
findings.body: span_count is set from the first union. If the second union is skipped, the count is correct. If the parent union runs, the count is overwritten, which is fine. However, when neither union runs, the count falls back to zcard, so this path is okay. The real problem is that the eviction cap is a hardcoded 1000 spans, while max_segment_spans=1001 in Python is now unused. Eviction with zpopmin removes the spans with the earliest end timestamps, which can include the root span, so segments silently lose data with no metric or log.

findings.title: __reduce__ passes redis_ttl positionally into segment_page_size
findings.body: The pickled SpansBuffer is rebuilt with (shards, timeout, root_timeout, redis_ttl). The fourth positional parameter of __init__ is segment_page_size, so after unpickling in multiprocessing workers, redis_ttl lands in segment_page_size and the real TTL resets to its default.

findings.title: No test for eviction behavior
findings.body: The new 1000-span eviction in add-buffer.lua is not covered by any test, so there is nothing verifying the cap or which spans are dropped.
